verses.text: I've seen something wrong under the sun, and it weighs heavy on people.

God gives someone riches, possessions, and honor, so they've got everything their heart could want. Yet God doesn't let them enjoy any of it, and a stranger gets to eat it all. It slips away like a breath. It's a terrible sickness.
Say a man has a hundred kids and lives a very long time. If he never gets to enjoy anything good and doesn't even get a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off.
The child comes and goes like a breath, leaving in darkness, with even its name hidden in the dark.
It never saw the sun or knew it, but it has more rest than that man.
Even if someone lived a thousand years twice over without enjoying anything good, don't they all end up in the same place?
People work to put food in their mouths, and their appetite still won't say it's had enough.
So what advantage does a wise person have over a fool? What does a poor person gain from knowing how to get along in the world?
Better to have what's right in front of you than let your desires wander everywhere. This too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists got its name long ago. What a human being is has already been made known. People can't go up against someone stronger than they are.
More words just give you more that slips away like a breath. What does anybody gain from that?
Who knows what's good for someone in this life, in all those fleeting days that pass like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they're gone?
